frequency_question: How often does the central bank introduce an iCRR or equivalent targeted liquidity absorption measure within a given multi-month horizon?
membership_rule: Includes any formal RBI announcement or directive implementing an incremental CRR on bank deposits to manage sudden liquidity surpluses. Excludes standard, routine changes to the baseline Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) or Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) that apply permanently rather than incrementally and temporarily.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named episodes; these represent the totality of incremental CRR usage in modern Indian banking history, as baseline CRR changes are excluded.
known_gaps: None; the instrument has only been utilized twice in modern monetary policy history as a temporary absorber.
skeleton: Ad-hoc liquidity surplus shock events requiring targeted deposit immobilization over a 26-year structural regime.
multiplier: 2 occurrences across 2 distinct liquidity-surge regimes (post-demonetization and post-pandemic normalization)
validity_reason: The monetary policy framework and central bank statutory powers regarding reserve ratios remain stable over multi-year horizons.
